entities.summary: Vijayanandi or Vijayananda was an Indian mathematician and astronomer who made significant contributions to trigonometry, flourishing during the 10th century CE in the medieval Indian subcontinent. His work, including the development of new mathematical models and astronomical tables, had a lasting impact on Indian mathematics and astronomy. Vijayanandi's achievements are also notable for their influence on Islamic mathematics and astronomy, which spread throughout the Middle East and North Africa. The Indian mathematician's legacy can be seen in the work of later scholars, such as Ulugh Beg, who built upon Vijayanandi's discoveries. Vijayanandi's contributions to trigonometry have also been recognized as a key milestone in the development of modern astronomy. The Indian mathematician's work, although largely forgotten in the West, has been rediscovered and reevaluated in recent years, highlighting the importance of Vijayanandi's contributions to the history of mathematics and astronomy.
